meta.subtitle: Three commands: html-doc init, html-doc build, html-doc serve. Zero flags. Designed so you mostly forget the CLI exists.
meta.summary: html-doc init / build / serve — what each does.

blocks.summary: init creates the docs/_kit symlink in your project. build produces dist/standalone/ + dist/site/ (each with their own site-manifest.json, llms.txt, page.md twins, plus Pagefind for site/ if installed). serve runs a local HTTP server and synthesizes stubs + manifest + llms.txt in memory — source dirs stay clean.
bullets: Source dirs hold JSON (or MD) only. Generated artifacts (stubs, manifest, llms.txt) never land in source.
build is idempotent; safe to re-run. dist/ is wiped each time.
serve synthesizes stubs and the manifest fresh on each request — no source writes.
Optional deps: pagefind (search index), jsonschema (page validation). Both soft-fail.

blocks.title: html-doc init
blocks.lead: One-time per project. Creates the docs/_kit symlink so pages can reference _kit/chrome.js etc.

blocks.source:
cd ~/path/to/your-project
html-doc init

# ✓ Linked /path/to/your-project/docs/_kit -> /path/to/html-doc
#
#   Reference the kit in your HTML <head>:
#     <script src="_kit/chrome-boot.js"></script>
#     <link rel="stylesheet" href="_kit/chrome.css">
#     <script src="_kit/chrome.js" defer></script>
#
#   Then run `html-doc build` to produce dist/standalone/ + dist/site/.

blocks.title: If docs/_kit already exists
blocks.content: Re-running init is safe — if the symlink already points at the kit, it prints "already linked" and exits 0. If it exists but points somewhere else, it errors and tells you what's there so you can decide.

blocks.title: html-doc build
blocks.lead: Walks the current directory, produces every dist artifact. Run before deploying dist/site/, before sharing dist/standalone/ files, or any time a search index needs to refresh. Source dir is never written to.

blocks.source:
cd ~/path/to/your-project
html-doc build

# ✓ Schema validation: 6 page(s) clean
# ✓ Wrote site-manifest + llms.txt under dist/{standalone,site}/docs/ (6 JSON page(s))
# ✓ Wrote 6 page.md twin(s) under dist/site/ + dist/standalone/
# ✓ Synthesized 6 stub(s) for pages without on-disk .html
# ✓ Pagefind index built: dist/site/pagefind/
# ✓ Built 6 HTML file(s):
#
#   standalone (inline, send-as-file):
#                file:///.../dist/standalone/docs/index.html
#                ...
#
#   site (shared assets, multi-page):
#   site root:   file:///.../dist/site
#                ...

steps.title: Walk *.json and *.md pages recursively
steps.content: Skips dist/, _kit/, node_modules/, .git/, venv/, __pycache__/. Treats files with kind:"page" (and any .md) as pages.

steps.title: Schema validation (optional)
steps.content: If jsonschema is installed (pip install jsonschema), every page is checked against kit-data/schema/page.schema.json. Errors print with field paths. Without jsonschema, prints a one-line hint and skips.

steps.title: build_standalone — single-file per page
steps.content: For each page, synthesize the HTML stub in memory, inline chrome.css/.js, chrome-boot.js, renderer.js, the page JSON, and the kit bundle. Output to dist/standalone/ with directory structure preserved.

steps.title: build_site — multi-page deployable
steps.content: Write a per-page stub + copy the source JSON to dist/site/ with directory structure preserved. Copy _kit/ and _kit-data/. Inject extracted text into hidden data-pagefind-body for indexing.

steps.title: Write site-manifest + llms.txt into both dist trees
steps.content: Generated alongside the pages they describe. The runtime's __htmldocDocsRoot + 'site-manifest.json' fetch resolves naturally.

steps.title: Pagefind index (optional)
steps.content: If pagefind is on PATH (brew install pagefind, or npx pagefind), run it over dist/site/. Output to dist/site/pagefind/. Soft-fails with install hint if absent.

blocks.title: build wipes dist/
blocks.content: build removes dist/standalone/ and dist/site/ before rebuilding so stale files don't accumulate. If you have anything else under dist/ you care about, move it out first. (You shouldn't.)

blocks.title: html-doc serve
blocks.lead: Local HTTP server in the project root. Synthesizes per-page .html stubs, site-manifest.{json,js}, and llms.txt in memory on each request — source dir stays clean. Picks the first free port from 9876.

blocks.source:
html-doc serve

# ✓ Serving /path/to/your-project on http://localhost:9876
#   Stop with Ctrl-C.
#
#   HTML files:
#     http://localhost:9876/docs/index.html
#     http://localhost:9876/docs/authoring.html
#     ...

items: Walks up from cwd to find the directory containing docs/_kit; serves from there. Run from anywhere inside the project.
First free port from 9876–9900. Caps at 9900 (if all taken, errors out).
Synthesizes /<docs>/<name>.html stubs from sibling .json or .md files on the fly; same for site-manifest.{json,js} and llms.txt. No filesystem writes.
Pagefind is not built by serve. Run html-doc build first if you need full-text search; serve falls back to in-page anchor search otherwise.
Opens the first HTML it finds in the default browser. Ctrl-C to stop.

content.content: Browsers apply different rules to local files than HTTP — symlink resolution, fetch, and ES module imports fail silently or behave inconsistently on file://. The local HTTP server sidesteps that. On macOS, opening a file:// URL also disables some same-origin policies that matter for the iframe sandbox in <live-snippet>. Always serve.

blocks.title: Optional flags
blocks.content:
--no-watch disables the filesystem watcher + live-reload (serve static only).
--no-search skips the background Pagefind index generation at startup. Both default to on so the dev loop is rich; opt out if you want a leaner serve.

blocks.title: Optional dependencies
blocks.lead: Two external tools the kit will use if present. Both soft-fail — install when you want the feature, skip when you don't.

cards.title: Pagefind — search index
content: Without it: search button still appears but says "Search index not found" when clicked.
With it: build adds a ~50–100 KB pagefind/ directory to dist/site/; the search button works on the built site.

cards.title: jsonschema — page validation
content: Without it: build prints a hint and skips validation.
With it: every JSON page validates against schema/page.schema.json on build; errors print field path + message. Catches malformed JSON earlier than the runtime.

blocks.title: Install + run
blocks.lead: Not in v2. Worth noting because they're frequently asked.

blocks.content: Two ways to invoke the CLI.

blocks.source:
uv tool install .
# Now `html-doc` is on PATH globally:
html-doc serve

blocks.content: Installs html-doc as a console script. The wheel packs chrome.{css,js}, schema/, glossary/, extrefs/, templates/ inside html_doc/assets/ so init/build find the kit assets without a git layout.

blocks.source:
uv run bin/html-doc serve
# Or plain python3 — both work:
python3 bin/html-doc serve

blocks.content: bin/html-doc is a thin shim that adds src/ to sys.path and runs html_doc.cli.main(). PEP 723 inline metadata pulls jsonschema into an ephemeral venv when invoked via uv.
